questions.question: Lui-Ngai- Ni is celebrated as a seed sowing festival by the people of ____________.

• It is celebrated on the 14th and 15th of February, marking the beginning of the spring season and the new year for the Nagas.
 
• The festival is a time to **celebrate the fertility of the land and to pray for a bountiful harvest.**
 
• The name of the festival comes from three different Naga languages:-
 
 
• **Lui (Mao language): seed**
 
• **Ngai (Rongmei language): festival**
 
• **Ni (Tangkhul language): sowing**
 
 
 
• The festival is celebrated in all the Naga inhabited areas in Manipur, however, the main festivity is hosted alternately at the Naga inhabited district headquarters namely Ukhrul, Tamenglong, Senapati and Chandel.

questions.question: net exports = total exports - _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**total imports.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net exports equal total exports minus total imports. **
 
• This value can either be positive (resulting in a trade surplus, where a nation exports more goods and services than it imports) or negative (resulting in a trade deficit, where a nation imports more goods and services than it exports).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Total Interest: **

 
 
• **It refers to the entire amount of financial remuneration that is earned over a specific period of time for lending money or other resources. **
 
• In the context of savings or an investment, it would be the sum earned over that period of time as a reward for investment.
 
• In terms of a loan, it would be the cost of borrowing that is paid to the lender.
 
 
 
• **Total Income: **
 
 
• **It is the aggregate amount of earnings generated by an individual or business. **
 
• For individuals, total income can include earnings from salaries, investments, rental income, business income, dividends, etc.
 
• For businesses, this would typically be the sum of all sales, before any deductions or expenses.
 
 
 
• **Total Revenue: **
 
 
• **It is a business term that refers to the total receipts from selling a certain quantity of goods or service. **
 
• It's an important part of a company's income statement and is often considered the "top line" figure as it sits at the top of the document.
 
• It's calculated by multiplying the price of the goods or services by the quantity sold.

questions.question: P, Q and R can complete a task in 20, 30 and 60 days, respectively. How many days will it take to finish the work if P is helped by Q and R every third day?

**Given:**

P can complete a task in 20 days,

Q in 30 days,

R in 60 days,

P is helped by Q and R every third day.

**Concept: **

Work done is reciprocal of the time taken. Use the concept of man-days.

**Solution:**

Total work = LCM(20, 30, 60) = 60 units

Efficiency of P = 60/20 = 3

Efficiency of Q = 60/30 = 2

Efficiency of R = 60/60 = 1

Work done by P in two days = 2 days × 3 = 6 units.

On third day, all three work together, their combined work = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 units.

Therefore, in every cycle of three days, work done = 6 + 6 = 12 units.

To finish 60 unit of work, days required = 3 × 5 = 15 days.

**Hence, it will take 15 days to finish the work.**

questions.question: If a natural number when divided by 2,3, and 4 leaves a remainder of 1 in each case, then what is the smallest possible three digit natural number?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the LCM of the given divisors: LCM(2, 3, 4) = 12.

The required number will be a multiple of 12 plus the remainder 1: (12 × k) + 1.

The smallest 3-digit multiple of 12 is 108 (since 12 × 9 = 108).

Add the remainder to this multiple: 108 + 1 = 109.

**∴ The correct answer is 109.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = 2, 3, and 4

Remainder = 1 in each case

**Formula Used:**

Number = LCM(divisors) × k + Remainder

**Calculations:**

⇒ LCM of 2, 3, and 4 = 12

⇒ The required number must be of the form 12k + 1

⇒ We need the smallest 3-digit natural number, so 12k + 1 ≥ 100

⇒ 12k ≥ 99

⇒ k ≥ 8.25

⇒ Since k must be an integer, the smallest possible value for k is 9

⇒ Required number = 12 × 9 + 1

⇒ Required number = 108 + 1 = 109

**∴ The correct answer is 109.**

LCM Remainder Concept (Same Remainder)

When a number is divided by x, y, and z and leaves the same remainder r in each case, the general form of the number is: LCM(x, y, z) × k + r

LCM Remainder Concept (Different Remainders)

When a number divided by x, y, and z leaves remainders a, b, and c respectively, and (x − a) = (y − b) = (z − c) = d, the number is of the form: LCM(x, y, z) × k − d

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: A × B = HCF × LCM

questions.question: A bus covered 60 km at a speed of 15 km/h, 100 km at a speed of 25 km/h and 20 km at a speed of 5 km/h. What is its average speed during the entire journey (in m/sec)?

**Given: **

The bus covered 60 km at a speed of 15 km/h,

100 km at a speed of 25 km/h, and 20 km at a speed of 5 km/h.

**Concept: **

Average speed = Total distance/Total time.

Total distance = 60 km + 100 km + 20 km = 180 km.

Total time = 60 km/15 km/h + 100 km/25 km/h + 20 km/5 km/h = 4 h + 4 h + 4 h = 12 h.

Average speed = Total distance/Total time = 180 km/12 h = 15 km/h

⇒ 15 × 1000/3600 = 25/6 m/sec

**Therefore, the average speed during the entire journey is approximately 25/6 m/s.**

Ashish's total wage = Rs. 70,

Kanika's total wage = Rs. 165,

Ashish's daily wage = Rs. 3.5,

Kanika's daily wage = Rs. 5.5.

**Concept: **

Total wage = Daily wage × Number of days taken to finish work.

Number of days taken by Kanika to finish work = Total wage/Daily wage = Rs. 165/Rs. 5.5 = 30 days.

Cost of the work = Daily wages of Ashish and Kanika × Number of days taken to finish work
